What this is

API Discovery & Governance

API Discovery & Governance starts by finding the interfaces (APIs) actually running in your environment, including undocumented, deprecated and partner-facing endpoints that no inventory records. Governance is what follows: classifying each API by data sensitivity and regulatory exposure, assessing its controls, and assigning ownership, standards, and lifecycle gates.

Questions We Are Asked

What is a shadow API?
An interface that is running and reachable but absent from the organization's catalog. The common sources are deprecated versions kept alive for one partner, internal services exposed during a migration and never withdrawn, endpoints generated by low-code platforms, and interfaces inherited through acquisition.
How do you discover APIs we don't know about?
By not relying on any single source. Gateway and DNS configuration, certificate records, traffic observation at the edge and between services, repository and specification scanning, cloud provider inventories, and partner integration contracts each surface a different subset, and the union is materially larger than any catalog.
Do you assess against OWASP API Security Top 10?
Yes. Findings are mapped to those categories, with weight given to the authorization failures that dominate real incidents (object-level, property-level and function-level authorization), alongside unrestricted resource consumption and unrestricted access to sensitive business flows.
Why is this an AI-related engagement?
Because an AI agent is only as contained as the tools it can reach. Once a model is given tool access, the API surface becomes a permission boundary, and an undocumented endpoint with weak authorization becomes reachable by a system that will find it faster than a person.
What do we get beyond a report?
A governance operating model: named ownership, a specification standard, a lifecycle with a deprecation path, and review gates positioned in the delivery pipeline rather than in a policy document. The register is delivered in a form that can be maintained.
